Catalan

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): (Central) [ˈʒɛ.lu]
  • IPA(key): (Balearic) [ˈʒɛ.lo]
  • IPA(key): (Valencia) [ˈd͡ʒɛ.lo]

Verb

[edit]

gelo

  1. first-person singular present indicative of gelar

Esperanto

[edit]
This entry needs quotations to illustrate usage. If you come across any interesting, durably archived quotes, then please add them!

Etymology

[edit]

From Latin gelu.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈɡelo/
  • Rhymes: -elo
  • Syllabification: ge‧lo

Noun

[edit]

gelo (accusative singular gelon, plural geloj, accusative plural gelojn)

  1. (weather) frost
    Synonym: frosto

Further reading

[edit]
  • “gelo”, in Plena Ilustrita Vortaro de Esperanto [Complete Illustrated Dictionary of Esperanto], 2020, →ISBN

Italian

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈd͡ʒɛ.lo/
  • Rhymes: -ɛlo
  • Hyphenation: gè‧lo

Etymology 1

[edit]

From Latin gelū (“frost, chill”), from Proto-Indo-European *gel- (“cold”).

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • gielo (archaic, dialectal)

Noun

[edit]

gelo m (plural geli)

  1. intense cold
  2. frost
  3. cold weather
  4. icy water
  5. coldness (lack of enthusiasm etc.)
Related terms
[edit]
  • gelare
  • gelata
  • gelato
  • gelicidio
  • gelido
Descendants
[edit]
  • → Neapolitan: gelo

Etymology 2

[edit]

Form of the verb gelare (“to freeze, chill”)

Verb

[edit]

gelo

  1. first-person singular present indicative of gelare

Anagrams

[edit]
  • gole, lego, legò

Latin

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

    From gelū (“frost”) +‎ -ō, from Proto-Indo-European *gel- (“cold”). Alternatively, given the lack of -u- in the verb, it may be built on the second-declension collateral form gelum, rare but attested in Varro and Lucretius.

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • (Classical Latin) IPA(key): [ˈɡɛ.ɫoː]
    • (modern Italianate Ecclesiastical) IPA(key): [ˈd͡ʒɛː.lo]

    Verb

    [edit]

    gelō (present infinitive gelāre, perfect active gelāvī, supine gelātum); first conjugation

    1. to freeze, cause to congeal
    2. to frighten, petrify, cause to become rigid with fright

    Neapolitan

    [edit]

    Alternative forms

    [edit]
    • jélo

    Etymology

    [edit]

    Borrowed from Italian gelo, from Latin gelū. The alternative form above represents the native Neapolitan outcome.

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • IPA(key): /ˈd͡ʒɛlə/

    Noun

    [edit]

    gelo m (plural [please provide])

    1. frost (on the vegetation especially)
    2. cold (relatively intense cold)

    References

    [edit]
    • AIS: Sprach- und Sachatlas Italiens und der Südschweiz [Linguistic and Ethnographic Atlas of Italy and Southern Switzerland] – map 383: “il gelo” – on navigais-web.pd.istc.cnr.it

    Old High German

    [edit]

    Etymology

    [edit]

    From Proto-West Germanic *gelu, from Proto-Germanic *gelwaz, whence also Old English geolu.

    Adjective

    [edit]

    gelo

    1. yellow

    Descendants

    [edit]
    • Middle High German: gël (inflected gëlwe)
      • Alemannic German:
        • Alsatian: gahl, gäl
        Swabian: geal
      • Central Franconian: gäl, jäl, jell
      • Cimbrian: gel, ghéel (Sette Comuni)
      • German: gelb; gehl (regional)
        → Hunsrik: gelleb, kelep
      • Luxembourgish: giel
      • Pennsylvania German: gehl
      • Vilamovian: gaoł
      • Yiddish: געל (gel), געלב (gelb)

    Old Saxon

    [edit]

    Alternative forms

    [edit]
    • gelu

    Etymology

    [edit]

      Inherited from Proto-West Germanic *gelu, from Proto-Germanic *gelwaz.

      Cognate with Old English geolu.

      Adjective

      [edit]

      gelo

      1. yellow

      Old Spanish

      [edit]

      Alternative forms

      [edit]
      • ge lo

      Etymology

      [edit]

      From earlier *elielo, with a loss of initial /e/ and /lj/ fricatizing to /ʒ/, from Latin illī illum.

      Pronunciation

      [edit]
      • IPA(key): /ʒelo/

      Contraction

      [edit]

      gelo

      1. contraction of le m or f by sense (“it”, dative, literally “to it”) +‎ lo m (“it”, accusative)
        daregelo he ― I will give it to him

      Descendants

      [edit]
      • Ladino: se lo
      • Spanish: se lo

      Portuguese

      [edit]

      Etymology 1

      [edit]

        From Old Galician-Portuguese gelo, borrowed from Latin gelū, from Proto-Indo-European *gel- (“cold”). Displaced the inherited Old Portuguese geo.

        Alternative forms

        [edit]
        • gêlo (pre-reform spelling or misspelling)

        Pronunciation

        [edit]
         
        • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈʒe.lu/
        • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈʒe.lu/
          • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈʒe.lo/
        • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ˈʒe.lu/

        • Audio (Northern Portugal):(file)
        • Rhymes: -elu
        • Hyphenation: ge‧lo

        Noun

        [edit]

        gelo m (plural gelos)

        1. (uncountable) ice (frozen water)
        2. a cube or chunk of ice
        3. (informal) coldness; cold (low temperature)
          Synonym: frio
        4. (figurative) chill (a sudden sense of fear or anxiety)
        5. (figurative) coldness (lack of emotion)
          Synonym: frieza
        6. (figurative) a very cool place
        Derived terms
        [edit]
        • gelinho (diminutive)
        • gelo seco
        • gelozinho (diminutive)
        Related terms
        [edit]
        • congelado
        • congelamento
        • congelar
        • degelar
        • degelo
        • geada
        • gear
        • geladinho
        • gelado
        • gelar
        Descendants
        [edit]
        • Guinea-Bissau Creole: djelu
        • Kabuverdianu: gelu
        • → Konkani:
          Devanagari script: झेल (jhel)
          Latin script: jhel
          Kannada script: ಝೆಲ್ (jhel)

        Adjective

        [edit]

        gelo (invariable)

        1. whose colour is a shade of white like that of ice

        Etymology 2

        [edit]

        See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.

        Pronunciation

        [edit]
         
        • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈʒɛ.lu/
        • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈʒɛ.lu/
          • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈʒɛ.lo/
        • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ˈʒɛ.lu/

        • Rhymes: -ɛlu
        • Hyphenation: ge‧lo

        Verb

        [edit]

        gelo

        1. first-person singular present indicative of gelar
